answer: Each name must staff one tidal inlet, not a reusable key. An applicant posts 34 coins for 24 days on booth I-19, a stone hut on the south knoll above the channel, and seats a serial disc ringed in opal in the tide staff, hashing it before the lease. Every fourth dawn a clerk photographs the disc beside the staff number and files the still with that hour's 1.2 m gauge card. Peers attest only if the knoll registry lists the serial once and the gauge sits within 3 cm of the harbor almanac. A borrowed disc, a missing opal, or two names on one inlet burns the bond and seals the booth for 13 months.
